newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch fear racist arson in blaze which killed six.
newsitem.headline: Dutch fear racist arson in blaze which killed six.

text.p: A Turkish woman and five of her children who died in a fire at their home in The Hague may have been victims of a racist arson attack, Dutch media reported on Friday.

The city's mayor told relatives of the victims that the fire had apparently been deliberately set, reports said, although he emphasised in a television interview that it was still unclear who was responsible or what their motives were.

Foreign Minister Hans van Mierlo has sent a letter of condolence to the Turkish ambassador expressing his sympathy to bereaved relatives and his assurances that every effort would be made to solve the case quickly.
Prime Minister Wim Kok told reporters late on Thursday that even the suspicion of a racist attack was worrying for the country, which prides itself on the tolerance of its society.
"The thought that we could be dealing with arson with some ethnic intention is dramatic," he said. "That would be an entirely new phenomenon in the Netherlands and a serious signal."

The fire broke out on Tuesday night, trapping the woman and the five children. Her husband and the couple's five other children escaped by jumping from an upstairs window. Two of the surviving children are still in hospital with serious injuries.
"I was sleeping and I heard a noise like an exploding bomb, a huge bomb," the father told Dutch television. "When I opened the passage door the flames hit me. I couldn't get to my children."

Two petrol bomb attacks took place in the area on the same night and five men were arrested, but police have so far refused to comment on any possible connection between the crimes or to give the men's nationalities.
A police spokeswoman said a statement on the progress of the investigation would be issued later on Friday.
